heading: The result
text: In the last 30 days, the KYC approval rate decreased by 5.4 percentage points, from 88.7% to 83.3%.
ARQ approved 2,945 fewer people than in the first 30 days.
Of these 2,945 approvals, 1,587 are because of fewer decisions and 1,358 are because of the lower rate.
Both countries show the decrease. Mexico decreased from 84.1% to 78.8%. Argentina decreased from 94.9% to 89.1%.

heading: What the data can show
text: The data has one decision record for each person, with a date.
The data does not show when a person starts KYC. Because of this, we cannot measure the completion rate.
This review uses the approval rate of recorded decisions. This rate is not the same as the completion rate.
CAUTION: Do not report the approval rate as the completion rate.

heading: Why the rate decreased
text: Four causes give most of the decrease:
Fraud signals: −2.05 points. The vendor found more images that look altered or fake.
Execution errors: −1.62 points. On Sep 1–2, some checks did not run, and the system rejected these people.
Selfie and liveness failures: −0.95 points. The vendor status page shows liveness incidents on Sep 1 and Sep 6.
Mexican documents with no document type: −0.60 points. The vendor did not identify these documents.
Face match failures decreased (+0.36 points). But face match is still a large cause of rejections.
CAUTION: A fraud signal is not confirmed fraud. Do not call it fraud before an analyst examines it.

heading: Short incidents
text: We found about 1,057 more failures than usual in four short date windows. The range is 1,055 to 1,130.
Aug 24, Argentina: more fraud signals and more traffic than usual.
Sep 1–2: execution errors in both countries.
Sep 1 and Sep 6: liveness failures.
Sep 14–19, Mexico: more fraud signals, with usual traffic.
The causes of these incidents are not confirmed. The vendor status page does not show an incident on Sep 2.

heading: Do these steps first (weeks 0–2)
text: Record each KYC start, each step and each final decision.
Hold each decision that has a TECHNICAL_ERROR. Do the check again before you reject the person.
Set alerts for sudden increases in failures.
Ask the vendor for incident reports for Sep 1, Sep 2 and Sep 6.
Examine a sample of fraud signals. Find which signals are real fraud.
Compare the control findings with the source systems. Correct the errors that you find.

heading: Then do these tests (weeks 2–6)
text: Test one guided retake for unclear selfies.
In Mexico, show pictures of the accepted documents before the capture.
If the fraud is confirmed, add device checks before the vendor call.

heading: The possible gain
text: If the tests work, ARQ can approve about 634 more people each 30 days.
The range is 233 to 1,093 people. This is 0.9 to 4.3 points of approval rate.
These numbers come from scenarios. They are not forecasts.

heading: Money
text: The value model uses market data. It does not use ARQ data.
With middle market values, the first-year value is $21 for each active customer. The cost is $13 for each active customer.
With cautious values, the value is $13 and the cost is $45. The cost is more than the value in the first year.
CAUTION: Replace the market values with ARQ values before you make a decision.

heading: Questions for ARQ
text: Does each row show the first attempt, the last attempt or the final decision?
Does ARQ have records of people who started KYC but did not send their documents?
What does the app do after a TECHNICAL_ERROR or a liveness failure?
Which vendor product and which data centre does ARQ use?
The answers can change the results of this review.
